Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop website composition option for Spironolactone Atlas.
Input image 1 is a VISUAL IDENTITY REFERENCE, not an edit target: preserve its deep ink ground #0B1020, off-white text #F3F0E8, coral #F48F7A primary emphasis, sparing teal #65B8AC navigation accent, Fraunces-like display serif, readable Inter-like body and tabular/JetBrains-Mono-like numerical annotations. Carry forward conventional clinical-editorial polish, thin rules, modest rounded corners and generous readable spacing. CHANGE THE COMPOSITION as described below. Do not copy the reference's centered hero or four equal outlined statistic cards.
Render one flat front-facing finished browser content screenshot without browser chrome, devices, design-process labels or perspective. Match the reference's LANDSCAPE desktop aspect, approximately 1487x1058. Show the opening and a useful glimpse into the next region. This must read as an educational website for pharmacy peers, not a poster or dashboard.
Top navigation: left small serif wordmark “Spironolactone Atlas”; right “The story”, “Reporting data”, “Evidence”, “Methods”, “Sources ↗”.
Only these verified reporting observations may appear: 24,805 selected reports; reporting window 2004–2025; Hyperkalaemia 3,452; Acute kidney injury 3,133; Hypotension 1,832; 52.2% no informative indication, 47.8% informative indication. Source text “openFDA · Retrieved 3 Nov 2026 · Selected cohort: 24,805 reports”. Reports can contain multiple reaction terms; this is not incidence or causality. No invented clinical claims, quotes, author identities, recommendations, approvals or evidence grades. No medication photos, anatomy, pills, molecule motifs or decorative science. Labels and values must be precise and legible.
COMPOSITION OPTION 2: EXPLANATION BESIDE EVIDENCE.
1. Slim full-width header about 80px tall, with a fine bottom rule and 56px side margins.
2. A two-column introduction between y135 and y650. Left 43%: small eyebrow “AN EDUCATIONAL EVIDENCE ATLAS”; display title “Spironolactone Atlas” across two balanced lines, about 76px with excellent serif character. Body at 21px “A guided look at uses, research evidence and adverse-event reporting.” Then actions coral “Read the story →” and outlined “Explore data”. Add a short quiet educational line, “Understand the story. Explore the sources. See the limits.”
3. Right 53%, unboxed on the continuous ink ground: heading “What appears in the reports?” at 32px serif, caption “Reported reaction terms in the selected cohort”. A professional horizontal bar chart with clear labels Hyperkalaemia, Acute kidney injury, Hypotension and respective right-end values 3,452 / 3,133 / 1,832. All bars coral, with the leading bar brighter and secondary bars quieter coral. Proportional lengths 100 /90.8 /53.1. Each full label sits above or beside its own bar with no overlap. Small denominator “Denominator: 24,805 selected reports”; caveat “Reports are not incidence or causality.”
4. Beneath both columns, one flat editorial metric strip separated by rules, no four card boxes: “24,805” above “Selected reports”; “2004–2025” above “Reporting window”; “52.2%” above “No informative indication”. Source line runs below, readable and not tiny.
5. The lower glimpse begins a quiet section “Read the evidence in context” in serif. Short line “Each observation has a source—and a limit.” Then a restrained row of text links “Uses and evidence →”, “Research activity →”, “Methods →”. Keep this lower region secondary to the opening chart and headline.
One dominant focal relationship: the title and its explanatory chart. Do not add unrelated graphics or a floating dock. Excellent real website hierarchy and alignment.

COMPOSITION OPTION 3: GUIDED CHAPTER READING.
1. Same slim header at 80px, 56px side margins.
2. Below header, a quiet left reading rail around 210px wide separated from the main content by a fine vertical off-white rule. Small mono heading “THE ATLAS”. Six accessible text chapter entries stacked with spacious rows: “01  Context”, “02  Uses and evidence”, “03  Reporting data”, “04  Research activity”, “05  Interactions”, “06  Methods and sources”. Active 03 marked by a short teal rule and explicit “Current chapter” label. This is conventional editorial navigation, no futuristic interface.
3. Main column starts x320, width about1100. At top y130: compact serif heading “Spironolactone Atlas” about62px, short body “Understand the evidence. Explore the sources. See the limits.” Two modest actions “Read the story →” coral and “Explore data” outlined, aligned left.
4. Thin rule around y330. Section eyebrow “READING THE REPORTS”. Large serif teaching question “What do the reports tell us—and what is missing?” at45px across two lines.
5. Main focal content below: left a very large tabular “52.2%” in off-white with coral short rule, label “No informative indication”. Label both segments immediately above or below and preserve exact 52.2:47.8 length ratio. No donut. This is measured data, not decorative geometry.

7. Lower glimpse of next region with serif heading “Explore the evidence” and a clean table header “Question    Population    Endpoint    Source”; no invented data rows.
The rail provides steady wayfinding; the main data lesson owns focus. Preserve calm conventional clinical editorial style, not Bauhaus or experimental grid. No big outlined statistic-card row, no bento, no decorative texture.
